chain_focus: AI-enabled drug discovery, precision medicine, autonomous laboratories, and the omics data platforms that feed biological models. The chain follows compute and cloud infrastructure into scientific software and AI-native discovery platforms, then into diagnostics, drug programs, and named biopharma customers.

players.product: AI-enabled molecular discovery programs

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Chris Boerner said that over the past several years 'BMS has embedded AI across its research and enterprise operations, demand for compute has grown alongside the scale and maturity of our AI capabilities.' In support of that expansion BMS 'recently announced partnership agreements with both Anthropic and NVIDIA.' Management said this will concretely help its scientists do three things: 'understand disease biology more deeply, design and test candidate molecules faster, and make earlier, better-informed decisions about which programs to move forward.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: AI is also being applied to clinical-development execution. Chief Medical Officer Cristian Massacesi said BMS now identifies and mitigates execution risk across every ongoing study - study design, statistical assumptions and comparator-arm performance - and described the work as 'integrating AI technology, data, and everything to have for each program this PTS improvement.' Separately, the 120 mg admilparant dose added to the phase III program was selected on the basis of 'modeling work, showing that there was a dose relation.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline productivity: management said the differentiated pipeline has 'the potential to introduce more than 10 new medicines by the end of the decade,' including iberdomide and mezigdomide, plus 'over 30 meaningful lifecycle management opportunities during that same period.' Ten products in the overall portfolio achieved double-digit growth in the quarter, and management said it continues to expect pivotal readouts across its therapeutic areas by the end of this year.
quarterly_data.figure: >10 new medicines by end of decade; >30 lifecycle management opportunities; 10 products with double-digit growth

quarterly_data.signal: Total revenue in the second quarter increased 5% year-over-year to approximately $13 billion. Growth portfolio revenue rose 14% to $7.6 billion, now representing nearly 60% of total revenue, with REBLOZYL up 29%, BREYANZI up 41%, CAMZYOS up 59% to $416 million and COBENFY up 81% to $63 million. ELIQUIS revenue was approximately $4.5 billion, up 21%. Gross margin was 71.4%, operating expenses were $4.1 billion, the effective tax rate was 16.5% and diluted earnings per share were $2.04.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue ~$13B (+5%); growth portfolio $7.6B (+14%), ~60% of total; ELIQUIS ~$4.5B (+21%); gross margin 71.4%; opex $4.1B; EPS $2.04

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue and adjusted diluted EPS was increased on first-half results, while maintaining projections for gross margin, other income and expense, and the tax rate. The revision incorporates projected ELIQUIS revenue growth of 20%-25% and a less pronounced total legacy portfolio revenue decrease now expected to be between 4% and 6%; operating expenses were raised slightly for accelerated pre-launch activities supporting the CELMoDs iberdomide and mezigdomide. Cash equivalents and marketable securities were approximately $11.5 billion, the company generated approximately $3.4 billion in operating cash flow and paid down an additional $1.2 billion in debt.
quarterly_data.figure: ELIQUIS growth 20%-25%; legacy portfolio decline 4%-6%; cash ~$11.5B; operating cash flow ~$3.4B; debt repaid $1.2B

quarterly_data.signal: Upcoming catalysts: BMS now expects the milvexian atrial fibrillation study to read out in the first quarter of 2027, and management disclosed the study needs to recruit 430 events for the primary endpoint of strokes and systemic embolisms and 530 events for bleedings before database lock. Admilparant in IPF is guided to read out by the end of this year with PPF a few months later, iberdomide has an August 17th PDUFA date, mezigdomide a May 13th, 2027 PDUFA date and CAMZYOS in adolescents a September 30th PDUFA date; COBENFY ADEPT top-line readouts now begin in early 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: milvexian Afib readout Q1 2027; 430 primary events and 530 bleeding events required; iberdomide PDUFA August 17th; mezigdomide PDUFA May 13th, 2027

players.product: AI-enabled antibody and drug discovery programs

quarterly_data.signal: Biomarker-driven patient identification kept scaling in neuroscience and oncology. Management said the number of p-tau217 blood tests more than doubled compared to Q2 2025 and that this is translating to more people being diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and accessing treatment. On the LIBRETTO-432 adjuvant selpercatinib result, which reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death by 83% versus placebo, Chief Scientific and Product Officer Dan Skovronsky said the effect size 'underscores the importance of comprehensive biomarker tests across all stages of disease.'
quarterly_data.figure: p-tau217 blood tests more than doubled year over year; selpercatinib recurrence or death risk -83% versus placebo

quarterly_data.signal: Genetic-medicine capability advanced on both the science and the manufacturing side. In the phase I-B study of VERVE-102, a gene-editing program designed to inactivate the PCSK9 gene, a single infusion reduced PCSK9 by 88% and LDL cholesterol by 62% at the highest dose. Lilly also opened its first dedicated genetic medicine manufacturing facility in Lebanon, Indiana, and produced the first batch of commercial material at its new site in Limerick, Ireland.
quarterly_data.figure: PCSK9 -88%; LDL cholesterol -62% at the highest dose; first dedicated genetic medicine manufacturing facility opened

quarterly_data.signal: R&D expenses increased 14%, driven by continued investment in the pipeline, including more than 40 active phase III programs. Management said business development is an important component of the R&D strategy and that 'the pace and average deal size have also continued to increase,' with agreements announced in the quarter to acquire Curevo, LimmaTech Biologics and The Vaccine Company, the acquisition of AtaiBeckley, and the completed Centessa acquisition adding cleminorexton in phase II.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D expense +14%; more than 40 active phase III programs

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue grew 48% compared to Q2 2025, with key products up almost $6.8 billion and the oncology, immunology and neuroscience medicines collectively growing 121%. MOUNJARO and ZEPBOUND combined for $14.9 billion of revenue and contributed $6.3 billion of growth. Gross margin was 86.3% of revenue, up approximately 1.3 percentage points, and non-GAAP performance margin was 54.8%, up nine percentage points.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue +48%; key products +$6.8B; oncology/immunology/neuroscience +121%; MOUNJARO+ZEPBOUND $14.9B (+$6.3B); gross margin 86.3%; performance margin 54.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Non-GAAP earnings per share were $8.38, including acquired IPR&D charges of $3.03, versus $6.31 in Q2 2025. Full-year guidance was raised: management increased the low-end of the revenue range by $3 billion and the high-end by $2 billion to $85 billion-$87 billion, with non-GAAP performance margin of 49%-50.5% and non-GAAP earnings per share of $35.50-$36.50.
quarterly_data.figure: EPS $8.38 (incl. $3.03 acquired IPR&D) vs $6.31; FY revenue $85B-$87B; performance margin 49%-50.5%; FY EPS $35.50-$36.50

quarterly_data.signal: Upcoming catalysts: with TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 complete, Lilly said it now has the clinical data package to support global registrations for retatrutide in obesity, obstructive sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis pain and plans to submit in the U.S. in quarter one 2027 under the BLA pathway. The first obstructive sleep apnea readout for Foundayo comes later this year, with an additional five ongoing phase III programs studying Foundayo, and EMBER-4 for INLURIYO is slated to read out next year in the adjuvant setting.
quarterly_data.figure: retatrutide U.S. submission Q1 2027; five additional ongoing Foundayo phase III programs

quarterly_data.signal: Head of research Mike Quigley said two external opportunities entered phase I in the second quarter, with internal projects to follow, and that 'This year alone, we plan approximately one new phase I start every two months, a meaningful step up as the changes in research take flight.' He also published an updated epidemiology data book providing the latest estimates across many indications represented in Sanofi's portfolio and pipeline.
quarterly_data.figure: ~1 new phase I start every two months; 2 external opportunities entered phase I in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: New CEO Belén Garijo made R&D productivity the central theme, saying the pipeline needs 'greater scientific rigor, fact-based decision making, a stronger, even if linear, governance, and more effective operations,' and launched a comprehensive outside-in portfolio review focused on the later-stage pipeline. Several phase III programs failed or were stopped in the quarter: two Dupixent studies in lichen simplex chronicus, the second venglustat study in Fabry disease and riliprubart in refractory CIDP stopped early on an IDMC recommendation. Itepekimab programs across COPD and chronic rhinosinusitis and balinatunfib programs were discontinued, and amlitelimab will not progress to regulatory submission.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Asked how much of the EUR 10 billion R&D budget is discovery versus development, Belén Garijo said 'The majority of the R&D budget is clinical development,' and Mike Quigley added 'there's not a linear relationship between spend and outcome,' emphasizing dynamic capital allocation away from unpromising medicines. Management expects moderate increases in R&D spend in the short term, growing at a lower level than sales. François Roger said Sanofi invested EUR 47 billion in BD and M&A over the last eight years and lost EUR 7 billion of it, and that BD and M&A activity will intensify to address pipeline weakness.
quarterly_data.figure: EUR 10B R&D budget; R&D to grow slower than sales; EUR 47B BD/M&A over 8 years, EUR 7B lost

quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter net sales grew 17.8% to EUR 11.6 billion, primarily volume-driven, with growth of around 15% restating for Dynavax and Blueprint. Dupixent grew 37% and exceeded EUR 5 billion of quarterly sales for the first time with more than 1.5 million patients under treatment; launch medicines grew over 60% and now represent 13% of sales; rare disease sales reached nearly EUR 1.9 billion, up 24%; vaccines declined 5% to EUR 1.15 billion, with Beyfortus up 54% to EUR 108 million and HEPLISAV-B up 43% pro forma to EUR 113 million. Business operating income rose 35.8% and business EPS grew 33.3%, or 21% underlying.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales EUR 11.6B (+17.8%); Dupixent >EUR 5B (+37%); launches +60%, 13% of sales; rare EUR 1.9B (+24%); vaccines EUR 1.15B (-5%); BOI +35.8%; business EPS +33.3%

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance was upgraded to sales growth of around 10% at constant exchange rates with business EPS growing slightly faster than sales; the full-year tax rate is now expected at around 21%. The combined 2030 ambition was raised by almost 10% on a like-for-like basis at constant exchange rates: Dupixent to about EUR 25 billion, pharmaceutical launches to about EUR 10 billion and vaccines to about EUR 9 billion, the vaccines cut split equally between currency and U.S. vaccination coverage rate dynamics.
quarterly_data.figure: FY sales +~10% CER; tax ~21%; 2030 Dupixent ~EUR 25B, launches ~EUR 10B, vaccines ~EUR 9B

quarterly_data.signal: Upcoming catalysts: the final phase III readout for Sarclisa in transplant-eligible multiple myeloma is expected in the remainder of 2026 and efdoralprin alfa phase II AATD emphysema data will support FDA discussions on a potential submission already in the second half. In 2027 Sanofi expects phase II-B results for brivekimig in hidradenitis suppurativa, frexalimab in relapsing multiple sclerosis, riliprubart versus IVIG in CIDP in the latter half of 2027, and pneumococcal and yellow fever vaccine readouts; frexalimab in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis reads out in 2028. Venglustat has U.S. priority review in type 3 Gaucher disease with a target action date of November 25th.
quarterly_data.figure: Sarclisa phase III readout 2026; venglustat PDUFA November 25th; frexalimab RMS 2027 and SPMS 2028; riliprubart VITALIZE H2 2027

Global CF revenue grew 11%, CASGEVY delivered $76 million compared with $30 million in Q2 2025 and JOURNAVX delivered $50 million compared with $12 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $3.3B (+12%); CF +11%; CASGEVY $76M; JOURNAVX $50M

Management said R&D accounts for nearly two-thirds of operating expenses and that the modest growth rate reflects redeploying dollars from programs that wind down to programs that are new or scaling up. Non-GAAP SG&A was $520 million, up 45%, and $21 million of acquired IPR&D expense was recorded in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D $889M (+1%); nearly 2/3 of operating expenses; SG&A $520M (+45%); acquired IPR&D $21M

In cystic fibrosis VX-828 recently completed dosing in the patient cohort, with VX-581 and VX-272 in healthy volunteer studies. The FDA also cleared the IND for VX-017, the type O or universal donor islet cell product, which management said would double the Type 1 Diabetes market opportunity from about 60,000 to about 120,000 patients.
quarterly_data.figure: 4 renal programs; VX-828, VX-581 and VX-272 next-gen CFTR correctors; T1D opportunity ~60,000 to ~120,000 patients

Interim analysis results from the AMPLITUDE phase III study in AMKD remain on track for early 2027, AMPLIFY results are expected this fall and initial VX-828 patient data in the second half of this year.
quarterly_data.figure: PDUFA November 30th; ~90% of renal field force with nephrology experience; AMPLITUDE IA early 2027

Management said the two lead assets, paltusotine and atumelnant, together represent a peak sales opportunity of about $5 billion, and expects the transaction to become accretive to non-GAAP operating income in 2029. Quarter-end cash and investments were approximately $13.6 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: $8.8B net of cash acquired; $4.5B term loan; ~$5B peak sales opportunity; accretive 2029; cash and investments ~$13.6B

Full year gross margin is expected to be just under 86% and combined non-GAAP operating expense guidance of $5.65 billion-$5.75 billion was reiterated, though now expected at the high end of that range. Guidance does not yet reflect the pending Crinetics acquisition.
quarterly_data.figure: FY revenue $13.1B-$13.2B; non-CF revenue >=$500M; gross margin just under 86%; opex $5.65B-$5.75B

quarterly_data.signal: Management cited external innovation as a core part of the strategy, describing 'our preclinical research collaboration with AbCellera, which leverages their T-cell engager platform to discover novel multi-specific antibodies' and saying the agreement 'directly complements our oncology expertise and supports our refined rare disease strategy.' In Q&A the CEO added that it is 'a preclinical collaboration looking at next-gen T-cell engagers, very early in our pipeline, but it directly aligns with our overall rare disease strategy, really expanding our focus on GI cancers.' The CFO said Jazz is deploying capital in a disciplined manner to enhance growth prospects, 'most recently with the AbCellera deal.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Non-GAAP adjusted SG&A and R&D expenses both grew 11%. The CFO said the SG&A increase was driven by higher expenses for Modeyso and Ziihera first-line GEA and, to a lesser extent, by 'investments in key commercial capabilities in digital and AI,' while the R&D increase was driven by higher clinical trial costs, primarily related to zanidatamab. Full year SG&A expense guidance was modestly increased, reflecting deliberate strategic investments behind XYWAV and Epidiolex and the rare disease strategy.

Modeyso generated $48 million in net product sales and more than 600 patients have been treated through the end of the second quarter. Management said it is actively working to establish reflexive biomarker testing across all gliomas and that updated NCCN guidelines now endorse liquid biopsy for the H3K27M biomarker, which it called a major milestone that broadens diagnostic pathways, reduces patient risk and accelerates time to treatment.
quarterly_data.figure: Modeyso $48M; >600 patients treated; NCCN endorsement of liquid biopsy for H3K27M

quarterly_data.signal: R&D programs are focused on building the next generation of growth drivers through internal innovation and external partnerships. Jazz is initiating three new Epidiolex clinical trials - a phase IV in adults with LGS, a phase III in a broad group of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and a seamless phase II-III of the capsule formulation in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy - building on a phase I-B in focal onset seizures and a phase I trial of JZP047, described as a novel molecular entity discovered by Jazz being developed in absence epilepsy. An NDA was submitted to the FDA for the novel capsule formulation.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 new clinical trials; JZP047 in phase I; capsule formulation NDA submitted

quarterly_data.signal: Record quarterly revenue was $1.21 billion, an increase of 16% over the second quarter of 2025, driven by 32% growth in the oncology portfolio, 13% growth in XYWAV to $471 million and 16% growth in Epidiolex to $292 million. Zepzelca grew 42% to $106 million and Ziihera generated $15 million while achieving more than 50% of the addressable market share in the U.S. in second-line BTC. XYWAV added approximately 525 net patients to reach approximately 17,125 active patients, more than 12% year over year growth.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $1.21B (+16%); oncology +32%; XYWAV $471M (+13%); Epidiolex $292M (+16%); Zepzelca $106M (+42%); Ziihera $15M

quarterly_data.signal: Full year 2026 total revenue guidance was raised to a range of $4.60 billion-$4.75 billion, with rare sleep revenue of $2.025 billion-$2.125 billion and double-digit XYWAV growth now anticipated after limited uptake of high-sodium generics. Non-GAAP adjusted EPS was $5.71 including IPR&D charges totaling $0.94; first half operating cash flow was $824 million and $2.2 billion of cash on the balance sheet supports continued business development, with one or more further deals still expected in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: FY revenue $4.60B-$4.75B; rare sleep $2.025B-$2.125B; EPS $5.71 (incl. $0.94 IPR&D); H1 operating cash flow $824M; cash $2.2B

quarterly_data.signal: Jazz is preparing for the August 25th PDUFA date for zanidatamab in first-line HER2-positive metastatic GEA and said it is highly confident of approval on or before that date. The phase III HERIZON-GEA-01 results were published in The New England Journal of Medicine, with a 26.4-month median overall survival in the zanidatamab plus tislelizumab arm, more than seven months longer than the trastuzumab control arm. Top-line results from the second interim overall survival analysis of the doublet are expected in 3Q 2026 and the Modeyso phase III ACTION overall survival interim analysis is now anticipated in the first half of 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: PDUFA August 25th; 26.4-month median OS (+7 months vs control); doublet second interim OS 3Q 2026; ACTION OS interim H1 2027

players.product: precision-oncology companion diagnostic programs

quarterly_data.signal: The phase III CLARITY-Gastric01 trial of sonesitatug vedotin demonstrated an overall survival benefit in patients with CLDN18.2 expression as low as 25% at any staining intensity, a lower threshold than that required by other CLDN18.2 targeted therapies. Dave Fredrickson said the company expanded the definition of CLDN18.2 positivity with a cutoff of greater than 25%, which represents about half of patients with gastric GEJ cancer, or more than 180,000 patients across the U.S., EU5, China and Japan. Management estimated peak year revenue of $3 billion-$5 billion for the ADC.
quarterly_data.figure: CLDN18.2 cutoff >25%; ~50% of 2L+ gastric patients; >180,000 patients; peak revenue $3B-$5B

quarterly_data.signal: Biomarker testing infrastructure was flagged as a commercial gating factor. For Truqap in PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer following the CAPItello-281 approval, management said 'a near-term priority is to establish testing in the setting, which today is not common practice.' Truqap revenue was $233 million in the quarter, up 37%. In the AVANZAR trial both the intention-to-treat and the TROP2 biomarker-positive populations sit at the top of the multiple testing procedure, so a positive study can come from either group. For Ultomiris in HSCT-TMA, discussions with health authorities are ongoing on interpreting the data 'including in the context of real-world evidence.'
quarterly_data.figure: Truqap revenue $233M (+37%)

quarterly_data.signal: Core R&D expense increased 6% in the first half and represented 23% of total revenue; management expects full-year R&D at the upper end of the low 20s percentage range as it builds out bispecifics, cell therapies and T-cell engagers. Capital expenditure was $1.5 billion in the first half and is expected to increase by around a third in 2026, including a new ADC manufacturing facility in Singapore, and the company opened a new Kendall Square R&D center in Cambridge. Deal-related payments totaled $3.3 billion and new BD transactions totaled just over $2 billion in upfront payments year to date.
quarterly_data.figure: core R&D +6%, 23% of revenue; H1 capex $1.5B, +~1/3 in 2026; deal payments $3.3B; BD upfronts >$2B YTD

quarterly_data.signal: Six high-value phase III programs read out positively in the first half, including first pivotal data for three new molecular entities, and the company secured 30 major market approvals. Pascal Soriot said 25 key phase III trial readouts are planned over the next 18 months, with pivotal data readouts for six new molecular entities in 2027 alone. Saruparib in prostate cancer was singled out as a $5 billion-range opportunity reading out next year.
quarterly_data.figure: 25 phase III readouts in 18 months; 6 NME pivotal readouts in 2027; 30 major market approvals in H1

quarterly_data.signal: First-half total revenue grew 6%, or 11% excluding Farxiga and Brilinta which are affected by generics, and core EPS grew 11%. Oncology total revenue grew 15% to $14.1 billion with the U.S. up 18% and Europe up 16%; Rare Disease grew 11% to $4.9 billion; BioPharmaceuticals declined 5% to $11.2 billion on loss of exclusivity for Farxiga, Brilinta and roxadustat. quarterly_data.figure: total revenue +6% (+11% ex-Farxiga/Brilinta); core EPS +11%; oncology $14.1B (+15%); rare disease $4.9B (+11%); BioPharma $11.2B (-5%); core gross margin 83%

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year guidance was reiterated: total revenue to increase by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core EPS by a low double-digit percentage at constant exchange rates. Management reaffirmed the risk-adjusted $80 billion revenue ambition for 2030, noting 11 approved new molecular entities against a target of 20 by 2030, and said it does not need additional business development to deliver post-2030 growth.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue mid-to-high single digit; core EPS low double digit CER; $80B by 2030; 11 of 20 NMEs approved

quarterly_data.signal: Management leaned on real-world and third-party data to evidence the Wegovy pill launch: 'a recently published study showed that weight loss in the real world exceeded that seen in the OASIS 4 clinical trial at the same point in time.' The U.K. launch was tracked using IQVIA sell-in data to private providers and pharmacies, which showed Novo Nordisk obesity market share rising from around 30% before launch to 45% in July, with around 300,000 patients started in three weeks. Novo now serves more than 46 million people living with obesity and diabetes, with around 1.5 million people on the Wegovy pill worldwide and over 5 million total prescriptions.
quarterly_data.figure: obesity share ~30% to 45% (IQVIA July sell-in); ~300,000 U.K. patients in 3 weeks; 46M people served; 1.5M on Wegovy pill; >5M total prescriptions

quarterly_data.signal: The ZEUS cardiovascular outcomes trial of ziltivekimab, with more than 6,300 people enrolled, failed to reduce MACE with a hazard ratio of 0.99 despite confirmed target engagement and reductions in free IL-6 and hsCRP. Martin Holst Lange framed it as a biomarker-causality test: 'There was a question on the correlation between the biomarkers and the actual outcomes, and that was the leap of faith that had to be tested.' For zenagamtide, an extra titration step was added and management said that 'from a modeling perspective, feel quite confident that we'll see a safety tolerability profile in line with what we've seen with, for example, CagriSema.'
quarterly_data.figure: ZEUS >6,300 patients; MACE hazard ratio 0.99; all-cause mortality hazard ratio 0.99

quarterly_data.signal: Novo invested more than DKK 26 billion into R&D and commercial activities in the quarter, received more than 10 regulatory approvals and started more than 5 clinical trials. The company-wide transformation is running ahead of plan on DKK 8 billion of savings, which are being reinvested into growth opportunities; full-time employees fell to around 66,700, a decrease of almost 12,000 or roughly 15% versus 12 months ago.
quarterly_data.figure: DKK 26B R&D and commercial investment; >10 approvals; >5 trials started; DKK 8B savings; ~66,700 FTEs (-12,000, -15%)

quarterly_data.figure: adjusted sales DKK 78.5B (+7% CER); obesity +16%; GLP-1 diabetes +2%; U.S. +4%; IO +10%; operating profit +11% CER; gross margin 78.2% vs 82.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Simulations Plus announced strategic collaboration programs with three large pharmaceutical companies to advance AI workflows across the drug development life cycle, using GastroPlus, MonolixSuite, ADMET Predictor and PKpluS. Management said there has already been a financial component to at least one relationship, that long-term commercial terms are still under discussion, and that AI is expected to become a contributor in fiscal year 2027 rather than fiscal 2026.
